method: Visible UI old session -> zero extra blocks; explicit Short / 96 kHz / +4 save; fresh defaults; explicit stopped restore
oldSession:
- heading "Rust graph worker prototype · M3e–M3j" [level=1]
- paragraph:
  - text: Six real instruments, explicit Rust mixing and kick-keyed compression. Choose a complete-graph worker or three source workers with a dependent Rust master. An AudioWorklet consumes fixed PCM buffer pools. This is a dry reference mix. The desk and its defaults remain on the
  - link "six-role comparison page":
    - /url: ./modular-ensemble.html
  - text: .
- paragraph: "Default pool: 4 × 1,024 frames, 256 KiB. Added buffering: 92.88 / 85.33 / 42.67 ms at 44.1 / 48 / 96 kHz. Missing audio becomes silence; expired blocks are discarded. No shared memory or cross-origin isolation required for this transport. Messaging can allocate and add jitter. Single-worker and three-worker timings are observational; no speedup is established."
- text: Sample rate
- combobox "Sample rate":
  - option "44.1 kHz"
  - option "48 kHz" [selected]
  - option "96 kHz"
- text: Buffering
- combobox "Buffering":
  - option "Default · 4096 frames" [selected]
  - option "Experimental · 2048 frames"
  - option "Experimental · 1024 frames"
- text: Worker scheduling
- combobox "Worker scheduling":
  - option "Timers · existing default" [selected]
  - option "Message tasks · experiment"
- text: Extra PCM headroom
- combobox "Extra PCM headroom":
  - option "None · original capacity" [selected]
  - option "+2 blocks · experiment"
  - option "+4 blocks · experiment"
- paragraph: Extra headroom adds ready PCM capacity and the same number of startup frames; the producer block size is unchanged. The exact buffering delay and memory appear below. M3j records source frames consumed between packet callbacks, not wall time or a device cause. Extra headroom remains opt-in.
- paragraph: Message-task scheduling is opt-in. It removes nested worker timers but did not remove Short / 96 kHz transport misses in the desktop trials; one Default trial also missed a quantum. No performance or audible-quality improvement is established. Serial playback has no source-worker scheduler.
- paragraph: 85.33 ms added buffering · 4 × 1024 frames · 768 KiB PCM for three workers. Live events must target the worker's next unrendered frame; dispatch time is additional.
- status
- button "Play worker mix"
- button "Play serial reference"
- button "Test serial fallback"
- button "Stop" [disabled]
- button "Inject 250 ms stall" [disabled]
- button "Play three-worker mix"
- button "Test pool fallback"
- button "Verify pool PCM · all rates"
- button "Compare one / three workers · 48 kHz"
- paragraph: "M3f groups: lead + bass, second + rhythm, pad + drums. Three workers own their source graphs; one Rust master in the worklet handles the dependent mixing and kick key. At the default profile, three fixed pools total 768 KiB with a 4,096-frame delay. Other profiles keep the same groups and processing. If any group is missing, all program/key inputs for that source frame are silent. Live event owners stay within one group. This prototype does not distribute arbitrary graphs or desk effects."
- button "Verify worker PCM · all rates"
- button "Verify all profiles · PCM"
- button "Measure buffering profiles · 48 kHz"
- button "Measure headroom · selected profile/rate"
- button "Save session locally"
- button "Load saved session" [active]
- paragraph: "Profile measurement takes about 3½ minutes at the selected sample rate: one full warmup per profile, then three measured repeats per profile in rotated order. Keep this page active and avoid other benchmark work. Missed/incomplete runs are retained. M3h measures contiguous ready source frames at quantum entry, per worker and coherent minimum, with planned final draining separate. This does not measure device crackles. Worker task times and optional worklet wall time have separate scopes; unavailable clocks are reported. Smaller profiles remain opt-in; the default stays 4096 frames."
- paragraph: "Playback is finite: 17.5 seconds plus declared buffering. Startup failure falls back to serial with the same buffering. A failure after playback starts stops this run; a fresh serial run is available above. Live controls must target frames the worker has not rendered yet. Reset/reload creates a new generation and graph."
- status: Pinned fixture/session restored. Audio stopped.
- generic: No run yet.
saved: Pinned fixture and selected profile/rate/scheduling/headroom saved. Audio stopped.
